scores.evidence: Applying the same Yjs update twice changes nothing, so duplicate delivery does no harm.
scores.rationale: Yjs/Hocuspocus behaviours, including the CRDT's inability to validate semantics and the limits of client-held edits, are stated accurately; the gap is thin treatment of rich-text merge semantics and tombstone compaction.

scores.evidence: Non-goals for the beta: native mobile apps, track changes or suggestion mode, permissions on parts of a document, end-to-end encryption
scores.rationale: The plan solves the real-time collaboration problem with offline, presence, sharing and versions. It has explicit exclusions with reasons and a realistic 12–14 week scope.

scores.evidence: The Sync Service owns document content... is the only writer of document state and versions. When the API Service needs to change content... it asks the Sync Service
scores.rationale: Ownership, data flows and interfaces are clear and applied consistently. There are minor loose ends, such as the 99.9% target against a single instance in M1 and version-restore mechanics.

scores.evidence: S1 fuzz: 100 runs × 10k ops, zero divergence between clients and saved state.
scores.rationale: Risk-specific spikes run early with go/no-go triggers, chaos and deploy-under-load tests, load tests and a production canary; thresholds are marked as assumptions.

scores.evidence: Assumption | Impact if wrong | How / when validated
scores.rationale: Assumptions are marked [A] with impact-if-wrong and a validation point for each, and the open questions name what would change the design.

scores.evidence: Saves fail. Sync keeps documents in memory, retries with backoff, emits `store_failures_total`, and an alert fires after 2 minutes.
scores.rationale: The major failures are covered with detection and recovery: crash, DB outage, revocation, hostile editor, schema skew, proxies. Poisoned or corrupt CRDT state and backpressure get less concrete handling.

scores.evidence: Each alert linked to a runbook and fired once in staging.
scores.rationale: The plan covers deploy, rollback, drain, metrics, canary, runbooks and on-call. Business-hours on-call against a 99.9% target is a mild gap.

scores.evidence: RDS about $300, Fargate (2–3 sync, 2 api) about $250, ElastiCache about $80, ALB about $40, so under $1k/month.
scores.rationale: The cost drivers are identified, labelled as rough, and controlled with a budget alert and a build-versus-buy rationale. Scaling behaviour and people cost are thin.
Every decision is rated for reversibility with revisit triggers. The hard ones (schema, CRDT format, permissions model) are spiked early, and the storage interface isolates D4.

scores.evidence: Redis is added in Milestone 2, only to relay messages between Sync Service instances.
scores.rationale: The plan starts with one instance and defers Redis, routing, comments, images and multi-region. The components are justified, and the pentest is reasonable for confidential documents.

scores.evidence: Changes plan if: any divergence is traced to Yjs or y-prosemirror rather than our code: pause M2 and evaluate ProseMirror's central-authority collab
scores.rationale: The plan gives a dependency-ordered task table with locations, done-when criteria, parallel tracks, a critical path and explicit pivot triggers.

checklist.evidence: Yjs; ShareDB (OT); ProseMirror's central-authority collab; build our own
Formatting conflicts follow the CRDT's deterministic rules.
10 headless clients doing random insert/delete/format, random disconnects, and server kills.
Saves with a debounce: 2 s after the last change, and at least every 10 s
exponential backoff and jitter, capped at 30 s... Hocuspocus Redis extension
Edits apply locally and are written to IndexedDB.
Every Sync instance closes that user's connections to the document with code 4403.
Undo affects only the user's own changes (the Yjs undo manager does this, and spike S2 verifies it).
Presence travels through the Yjs awareness channel and is never saved.
M1: First end-to-end slice + core risks... Out: sharing UI, presence, offline cache, multiple instances.
50 simulated editors at 2 ops/s on one 1 MB doc... 1 MB per message, 10 MB per document
Raise `MIN_CLIENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` in Sync config, then enable creating the node.

traps.evidence: Co-editing with no conflict dialogs... Resolve concurrent edits with Yjs (CRDT)
We do not write our own OT.
In: login, create/open doc, co-edit, save to Postgres, CI/CD to staging
Each client sends the updates the server is missing... refusing to unload a document with unsaved changes.
a CRDT can't check edits for meaning on the server side

note: An unusually strong, well-sequenced Yjs-based plan with early risk spikes and explicit reversibility; its weak spots are the persistence design (debounced full-state saves, no append-only log or compaction) and shallow rich-text merge semantics.
